stages.answer_line: Recommended opening definition: Cārvāka (Indian materialist school), also called Lokāyata (worldly doctrine), is a non-Vedic and this-worldly philosophy that accepts pratyakṣa (perception) as the only independent pramāṇa (means of valid knowledge) and rejects unverifiable transcendent entities; because its primary texts are lost, its doctrines must be stated as a cautious doxographical reconstruction.
source_references: Historical Reconstruction and the Source Problem

stages.answer_line: Cārvāka (Indian materialist school) epistemology treats pratyakṣa (perception) as the only independent pramāṇa (means of valid knowledge), while accepting inference only as fallible practical expectation rather than certain knowledge.
